paragraphs.sourceText: Science of 瞬tba心：How failure can屿10\le career prospects
paragraphs.translationZh: 瞬息万变的心之学：失败如何影响屿10\le的职业前景

paragraphs.sourceText: A) How do early career setbacks affect our long-term success? Failures can help us learn and overcome our fears. But disasters can still wound us. They can screw us up and set us back. Wouldn't it be nice if there was genuine, scientifically documented truth to the expression "what doesn't kill you makes you stronger''?
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 早期职业挫折如何影响我们的长期成功？失败可以帮助我们学习并克服恐惧。但灾难仍然会伤害我们。他们可以把我们搞砸，让我们倒退。如果“杀不死你的会让你变得更坚强”这句话是真实的、有科学依据的，那不是很好吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: B) One way social scientists have probed the effects of career setbacks is to look at scientists of very similar qualifications. These scientists, for reasons that are mostly arbitrary, either just missed getting a research grant or just barely made it. In social sciences, this is known as examining "near misses" and "narrow wins" in areas where merit is subjective. That allows researchers to mea亚e only the effects of being chosen or not. Studies in this area have found conflicting results. In the competitive game of biomedical science, research has been done on scientists who narrowly lost or won grant money. It suggests that narrow winners become even bigger winners down the line. In other words, the rich get richer.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 社会科学家探究职业挫折影响的一种方法是观察具有非常相似资历的科学家。这些科学家，由于大多是任意的原因，要么错过了研究资助，要么勉强获得。在社会科学中，这被称为在主观的领域检查“侥幸”和“险胜”。这使得研究人员可以仅衡量被选择或不被选择的影响。该领域的研究发现了相互矛盾的结果。在生物医学科学的竞争中，人们对以微弱优势输掉或赢得资助的科学家进行了研究。这表明，微弱的赢家最终会成为更大的赢家。换句话说，富人变得更富。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) A 2018 study published in the Proceedi鸣'S of the National Academy of Sciences, for example, followed researchers in the Netherlands. Researchers concluded that those who just barely qualified for a grant were able to get twice as much money within the next eight years as those who just missed out. And the narrow winners were 50 percent more likely to be given a professorship.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 例如，2018 年发表在美国国家科学院 Proceedi鸣'S 上的一项研究跟踪了荷兰的研究人员。研究人员得出的结论是，那些勉强有资格获得资助的人在未来八年内获得的资金是那些刚刚错过资助的人的两倍。而以微弱优势获胜的人获得教授职位的可能性高出 50%。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Others in the US have found similar effects with National Institutes of Health early-career fellowships launching narrow winners far ahead of close losers. The phenomenon is often referred to as the Matthew effect, inspired by the Bible's wisdom that to those who have, more will be given. There's a good explanation for the phenomenon in the book匹Formula: The Universa.l La泗of Success by Albert Laszlo Barabasi. According to Barabasi, it's easier and less risky for those in positions of power
paragraphs.translationZh: D）美国的其他人也发现了类似的效果，美国国立卫生研究院的早期职业奖学金推出了微弱的赢家，远远领先于势均力敌的输家。这种现象通常被称为马太效应，其灵感来自于圣经的智慧，即拥有者，将得到更多。艾伯特·拉斯洛·巴拉巴西 (Albert Laszlo Barabasi) 所著的《匹方程式：成功的宇宙》一书中对这一现象有很好的解释。巴拉巴西认为，对于那些掌握权力的人来说，这更容易、风险更小

paragraphs.sourceText: E) This is bad news for the losers. Small early career setbacks s氏m to have a disproportionate effect down the line. What didn't kill them made them weaker. But other studies using the same technique have shown there's sometimes no penalty to a near miss. Students who just miss getting into top high schools or universities do just as well later in life as those who just manage to get accepted. In this case, what didn't kill them simply didn't matter. So is there any evidence that setbacks might actually improve our career prospects? There is now.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 这对于失败者来说是个坏消息。早期职业生涯中的小挫折可能会对以后产生不成比例的影响。那些没有杀死他们的东西只会让他们变得更弱。但使用相同技术的其他研究表明，有时侥幸成功并不会受到任何惩罚。那些错过进入顶尖高中或大学的学生在以后的生活中和那些刚刚被录取的学生一样好。在这种情况下，没有杀死他们的东西根本不重要。那么有没有证据表明挫折实际上可以改善我们的职业前景呢？现在有了。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) In a study published in Nature Communications, Northwestern University sociologist Dashun Wang tracked more than 1, 100 scientists who were on the border between getting a grant and missing out between 1990 and 2005. He followed various measures of performance over the next decade. These included how many papers they authored and how influential those papers were, as measured by the number of subsequent citations. As expected, there was a much higher rate of attrit加（减员）among scientists who didn't get grants. But among those who stayed on, the close losers performed even better than the narrow winners. To malce sure this wasn't by chance,'Wang conducted additional tests using different performance measures. He examined how many times people were first authors on influential studies, and the like.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 在《自然通讯》上发表的一项研究中，西北大学社会学家王大顺追踪了 1, 100 多名在 1990 年至 2005 年间处于获得资助和错过资助边缘的科学家。他跟踪了接下来十年的各种绩效衡量标准。其中包括他们撰写的论文数量以及这些论文的影响力（通过后续引用的数量来衡量）。正如预期的那样，没有获得资助的科学家的减员率要高得多。但在那些留下来的人中，那些势均力敌的失败者的表现甚至比微弱的获胜者还要好。为了确保这不是偶然的，王使用不同的性能指标进行了额外的测试。他检查了人们有多少次成为有影响力的研究的第一作者等等。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) One straightforward reason close losers might outperform narrow winners is that the two groups have comparable ability. In Wang's study, he selected the most determined, passionate scientists from the loser group and culled (剔除）what he deemed the wealcest members of the winner group. Yet the persevering losers still came out on top. He thinks that being a close loser m烛t give people a psychological boost, or the proverbial kick in the pants.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 势均力敌的失败者可能比微弱的获胜者表现更好的一个直接原因是，两组的能力相当。在王的研究中，他从失败者群体中挑选了最坚定、最热情的科学家，并剔除了他认为胜利者群体中最富裕的成员。然而，坚持不懈的失败者仍然名列前茅。他认为，作为一个接近的失败者，不会给人带来心理上的鼓舞，或者众所周知的“踢裤子”。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Utrecht University sociologist Arnout van de Rijt was the lead author on_ the 2018 paper showing the rich get richer. He said the new finding is apparently reasonable and worth some attention. His own work showed that although the narrow winners did get much more money in the near future, the actual performance of the close losers was just as good.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 乌得勒支大学社会学家 Arnout van de Rijt 是 2018 年论文的主要作者，该论文显示富人变得更富有。他表示，这一新发现显然是合理的，值得关注。他自己的研究表明，尽管微弱的获胜者在不久的将来确实获得了更多的钱，但接近的失败者的实际表现也同样好。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) He said the people who should be paying regard to the Wang paper are the funding agents who distribute government grant money. After all, by continuing to pile riches on the narrow winners, the taxpayers are not getting the maximum bang for their buck if the close losers are performing just as well or even better. 36. Being a close loser could greatly motivate one to persevere in their research.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 成为一名接近失败者可以极大地激励一个人坚持研究。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Grant awarders tend to favor researchers already recognized in their respective fields.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 资助者倾向于青睐在各自领域已得到认可的研究人员。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Suffering early setbacks might help people improve their job performance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 早期遭受挫折可能有助于人们提高工作绩效。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Research by social scientists on the effects of career setbacks has produced contradictory findings.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 社会科学家对职业挫折影响的研究得出了相互矛盾的结果。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. It is not to the best interest of taxpayers to keep giving money to narrow winners.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 继续向少数获胜者提供资金并不符合纳税人的最佳利益。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Scientists who persisted in research without receiving a grant made greater achievements than those who got one with luck, as suggested in one study.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 正如一项研究表明，没有获得资助而坚持研究的科学家比那些幸运获得资助的科学家取得了更大的成就。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. A research paper rejected by one journal may get accepted by another.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 一篇被一家期刊拒绝的研究论文可能会被另一家期刊接受。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. According to one recent study, narrow winners of research grants had better chances to be promoted to professors.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 根据最近的一项研究，研究补助金的少数获得者有更好的机会晋升为教授。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. One researcher suggests it might be more fruitful to distribute grants on a relatively equal basis.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 一位研究人员认为，在相对平等的基础上分配赠款可能会更有效。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Minor setbacks in their early career may have a strong negative effect on the career of close losers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 早期职业生涯中的小挫折可能会对那些接近失败者的职业生涯产生强烈的负面影响。

paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: well as mental health. It is found that people are more creative following·the completion of a tedious task. When people are bored, they have an increase in "associative thought"一the process of making new connections between ideas, which is linked to innovative thinking. These studies are impressive, but in reality, the benefits of boredom may be related to having time to clear your mind, be quiet, or daydream.
paragraphs.translationZh: 以及心理健康。研究发现，人们在完成一项乏味的任务后会变得更有创造力。当人们感到无聊时，他们的“联想思维”就会增加，即在想法之间建立新联系的过程，这与创新思维有关。这些研究令人印象深刻，但实际上，无聊的好处可能与有时间理清思绪、保持安静或做白日梦有关。

paragraphs.sourceText: In our stimulation-rich world, it seems unrealistic that boredom could occur at all. Yet, there are valid reasons boredom may feel so p血ul. As it turns out, boredom might signal the fact that you have a need that isn't being met.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在我们这个充满刺激的世界里，出现无聊似乎是不现实的。然而，无聊让人感到如此充满活力是有充分理由的。事实证明，无聊可能表明你的需求没有得到满足。

paragraphs.sourceText: Our always-on world of social media may result in more connections, but they are superficial and can get in the way of building a real sense of belonging. Feeling bored may signal the desire for a greater sense of community and the feeling that you fit in with others around you. So take the step of joining an organization to build face-to-face relationships. You'll find depth that you won't get from your screen no matter how many likes you get on your post.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们永远在线的社交媒体世界可能会带来更多的联系，但它们是肤浅的，可能会妨碍建立真正的归属感。感到无聊可能表明你渴望获得更大的社区意识以及与周围其他人融为一体的感觉。因此，采取加入组织的步骤来建立面对面的关系。无论您的帖子获得多少赞，您都会发现屏幕上无法提供的深度。

paragraphs.sourceText: Similar to the need for belonging, bored people often report that they feel a limited sense of meaning. It's a fundamental human need to have a larger purpose and to feel like we're part of something bigger than ourselves. When people are bored, they're more likely to feel less meaning in their lives. If you want to reduce boredom and increase your sense of meaning, seek work where you can make a unique contribution, or find a cause you can support with your time and talent.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与归属感的需求类似，无聊的人经常表示他们感觉意义有限。人类的基本需求是拥有更大的目标，并感觉自己是比自己更伟大的事物的一部分。当人们感到无聊时，他们更有可能感到生活没有意义。如果您想减少无聊并增加意义感，请寻找可以做出独特贡献的工作，或者找到可以用您的时间和才能支持的事业。

paragraphs.sourceText: If your definition of boredom is being quiet, mindful, and reflective, keep it up. But if you're struggling with real boredom and the emptiness it provokes, consider whether you might seek new connections and more significant challenges. These are the things that will genuinely relieve boredom and make you more effective in the process.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果你对无聊的定义是安静、专注和反思，那就继续下去吧。但如果你正在与真正的无聊及其引发的空虚作斗争，请考虑是否可以寻求新的联系和更重大的挑战。这些事情能够真正缓解无聊，让你在这个过程中更加高效。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Can you remember what you ate yesterday? If asked, most people will be able to give a vague description of their main meals: breakfast, lunch, dinner. But can you be sure you've noted every snack bar in your car, or every handful of nuts at your desk? Most people will have a feeling that they've missed something out.
paragraphs.translationZh: 你还记得昨天吃了什么吗？如果被问到，大多数人都能模糊地描述他们的主餐：早餐、午餐、晚餐。但你能确定你已经注意到你车里的每一块小吃店，或者你办公桌上的每一把坚果吗？大多数人都会有一种感觉，他们错过了一些东西。

paragraphs.sourceText: We originally had this suspicion back in 2016, puzzled by the fact that national statistics showed calorie consumption falling dramatically over past decades. We found reliable evidence that people were drastically under-reporting what they ate.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们最初在 2016 年就有过这种怀疑，当时国家统计数据显示过去几十年来卡路里消耗量急剧下降，这让我们感到困惑。我们发现可靠的证据表明人们严重少报了自己的饮食情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now the Office for National Statistics has confirmed that we are consuming 50% more calories than our national statistics claim.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，国家统计局已证实，我们消耗的卡路里比国家统计数据声称的多 50%。

paragraphs.sourceText: Why is this happening? We can point to at least three potential causes. One is the rise_ in obesity levels itself. Under-reporting rates are much higher for obese people, because they simply consume more food, and thus have more to remember.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么会发生这种情况？我们可以指出至少三个潜在原因。一是肥胖水平本身的上升。肥胖者的漏报率要高得多，因为他们只是消耗了更多的食物，因此需要记住更多的东西。

paragraphs.sourceText: Another cause is that the proportion of people who are trying to lose weight has been increasing over time. People who want to lose weight are more 1ilcely to under-report their eating—regardless of whether they are overweight or not. This may be driven partly by self-deception or "wishful thinkin旷
paragraphs.translationZh: 另一个原因是，随着时间的推移，尝试减肥的人比例一直在增加。想要减肥的人更容易少报自己的饮食情况——无论他们是否超重。这可能部分是由于自欺欺人或“一厢情愿”

paragraphs.sourceText: The final potential cause is an increase in snacking and eating out over recent decades—both in terms of how often they happen and how much they contribute to our overall energy intake. Again, there is evidence that food consumed out of the home is one of the most poorly recorded categories in surveys.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最后一个潜在原因是近几十年来吃零食和外出就餐的增加——无论是发生的频率还是它们对我们整体能量摄入的贡献程度。同样，有证据表明，家庭外消费的食物是调查中记录最差的类别之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: So, what's the message conveye .d? For statistics, we should invest m more accurate measurement options. For policy, we need to focus on options that make it easy for people to eat fewer calories. If people do not know how much they are eating, it can be really hard for them to stick to a diet. Also, we should be looking for new ways to ensure what people eat wouldn't have much impact on their waistlines. If this works, it won't matter if they can't remember what they ate yesterday.
paragraphs.translationZh: 那么，.d 传递的消息是什么？对于统计，我们应该投资更准确的测量选项。在政策方面，我们需要关注那些能让人们轻松摄入更少卡路里的选择。如果人们不知道自己吃了多少，他们就很难坚持节食。此外，我们应该寻找新的方法来确保人们的饮食不会对他们的腰围产生太大影响。如果这有效的话，即使他们不记得昨天吃了什么也没关系。
